statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 65 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 36 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence declines from 65 to a 60 floor purely because the reference tape ages rather than because the evidence has become conflicting. No danger window is published, because the first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist falls about two hours after the end of this forecast.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 24: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, the 10-year near 4.72% and a coin-flip September Fed meeting after Warsh; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about two hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range against a 29,695.75 previous close; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 12 basis points to roughly 4.38 percent and the 10-year closed near 4.72 percent, while the Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, and September rate-hike odds were repriced to roughly 55 to 57 percent from about 35 percent, leaving the meeting described in current reporting as close to a coin flip. The decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor industry fell 2.91 percent and semiconductor equipment 3.96 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Sector context was split, with Technology about 1.4 percent lower against Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical each about 1.4 percent higher. Commodities were re-verified this run with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars after a roughly four percent weekly decline, with no verified new Middle East supply discontinuity; gold remained sharply lower, consistent with a real-rate driven repricing rather than a growth scare. The shared cross-asset context file read this run was collected at 17:56 UTC and is now about 150 minutes old, past its 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale and used only as composition confirmation for the independently verified Friday session, explicitly not as live price-path evidence. Weekend headline flow through the assessment cutoff has been thematic, dominated by commentary on the Federal Reserve's communication and rate path and on AI infrastructure, with no verified geopolitical or policy discontinuity. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path rather than the probability of a large move, and no path of any kind can exist inside a scheduled halt, Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots. The genuine open questions - how the reopen prices a hawkish Fed repricing, and how the 1 to 4 September data stack lands - are carried in Stress, which ramps from 25 to 36 within the moderate band, and in Confidence, which eases from 65 to a 60 floor as the reference tape ages past forty hours.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final hour of Friday's cash session, the post-close futures hour, and hours one through twenty-three of the weekend halt. The mode was mixed as the Jackson Hole keynote was digested into the 20:00 UTC close, with Tail 12 and Stress 52 in that block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH at any point because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the close the mode settled to normal and Tail decayed to 5, where it has stayed for every subsequent hour. Stress fell from 52 to a 22 to 25 plateau, and Confidence declined steadily from 88 to 66 as the reference tape aged rather than because evidence became conflicting. No hour in the window is unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress ramps from 25 to 36 in the moderate band, rising with the stock of unpriced weekend information ahead of a reopen at Sunday 22:00 UTC that falls about two hours after the final slot, and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom results, ISM Services and the August payrolls report. Confidence eases from 65 to a 60 floor, staying in the solid band because the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified even as the reference tape ages past forty hours by the end of the window.
